clue.text: Getting bad news, so yell — such lack of fortitude!

indicators.note: bad here says the words before and after it are in a poor state and must be jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who shrieks on hearing bad news is mocked for having no backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting bad' signals that NEWS, SO and YELL are scrambled together; 'such' just points the whole clue at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, so the quality of being yellow is cowardice, a want of courage.

clue.text: Vehicle reversing in an enclosed space

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the vehicle's name from back to front

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads, traditionally a brewer's

explanation.surface: A car backing up inside a fenced-off area.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard or walled patch of ground beside a building is called by this name.

clue.text: Awful mumbler — a northern feller

indicators.note: awful suggests the word mumbler is botched and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful mutterer turns out to be a fellow from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' reads as dialect for a man, but here it is one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A logger cuts down trees, so a tree-feller is exactly what this worker is.

clue.text: Look up about practice available for a winger

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look!
use can mean custom or practice, as in 'in common use'

explanation.surface: Someone told to check what training is on offer for a wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' in a down clue turns the first piece; 'winger' suggests a footballer but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is an old name for the blackbird or ring ouzel, a bird and so a creature with wings.

clue.text: Counts as a scriptural book

explanation.surface: Something tallied ranks as holy scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Counts as a noun are tallies or figures; the fourth book of the Old Testament also bears this name.

clue.text: Tasted power in conveyance over the snow

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a sled is a sledge for travelling over snow
amp, short for ampere or amplifier, stands for electrical power here

explanation.surface: Someone tried strength while riding a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To try a small portion of food or drink is to test it, which is what tasting means.

clue.text: Mark the skinhead has personal transport

parts.note: the head of the word skin is its first letter
a car is a private vehicle

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed youth with his own vehicle is a marked man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' is read as the head of 'skin', its first letter, not a shaven youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish left on the skin by a healed wound is a lasting trace.

clue.text: Preserve a lake or other stretch of water

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Protect a lake or some other body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made waterway is a long channel, unlike a lake.

clue.text: Dries hops a new way. Speak with great enthusiasm of it

indicators.note: a new way says the letters before it are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for an improved method of drying hops, with someone gushing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' of 'hops a new way' is part of the jumble; the indicator is 'new way'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave or wax lyrical about something is to go into effusive praise.

clue.text: The old soldier is more earthy about sex-appeal

indicators.note: about says the earthier word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: cruder means coarser, more earthy in humour
SA is the abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A veteran trooper is rather vulgar about allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old soldier' is a medieval warrior of the Holy Land campaigns, not a veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight who fought in the medieval holy wars was a fighting man of long ago.

clue.text: One of the twins composing a piece of mediocre music

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A twin is writing a dull bit of music.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend the city's founders were brothers suckled by a wolf, and this is Romulus's sibling.

clue.text: The well-organised Roman made notes

indicators.note: well-organised says the letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An efficient Roman produced written reminders.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a written reminder, a record of points to be remembered.

clue.text: Surprise expressed at sources of drinking-water

explanation.surface: Astonishment at finding springs to drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment; also two shafts sunk to draw up water.

clue.text: Sarah is backing him

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the whole run from right to left

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of Sarah
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sarah supports a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support but turns the whole run round, so the reversal of a short Sarah plus 'is' gives a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so a male person referred to as him.

clue.text: An antelope — sound healthy animal

indicators.note: sound says we hear the phrase rather than read it

parts.note: hearty means robust and healthy, and a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: An African grazer is a fit creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a synonym for healthy, but it signals that HEARTY BEAST is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African grazing species with long face and curved horns belongs to the antelope family.

clue.text: Inoffensive, without aspiration, though short of members

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy h sound, so without it the H goes

parts.note: harmless means doing no harm, inoffensive

explanation.surface: Someone harmless and unambitious, though lacking limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without aspiration' reads as unambitious but means losing the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Members are limbs, so lacking upper limbs leaves one short of them.

clue.text: The basic necessity for a suit

definitions.text: The basic necessity for a suit

parts.words: The basic necessity for a suit
parts.note: suit suggests clothing, but here a lawsuit, which cannot succeed without proof

explanation.definitionFit: Proof brought before a court is what any legal case depends on.

clue.text: Inferred a French nobleman should go into action

indicators.note: should go into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat ought to get moving, someone concluded.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reach a conclusion by reasoning.

clue.text: Landseer's resort when all at sea?

definitions.text: Landseer's resort when all at sea?

parts.words: Landseer's resort when all at sea?
parts.note: Landseer suggests the Victorian painter, but read it as a land-seer, the lookout who sits aloft on a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The lookout platform at the top of a ship's mast is where the sailor scanning for land sits.

clue.text: Having some inclination for nursing

explanation.surface: Somewhat inclined to care for the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a leaning towards something; also looking after a patient.

clue.text: Dispute win for example

parts.note: to gain is to win
say introduces an example, as in 'a fruit, say an apple'

explanation.surface: Argue about a victory, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or deny something is to dispute it.

clue.text: A scoundrel promises to pay? That's unusual!

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt, so IOUS is the plural

explanation.surface: A rogue offering written pledges of payment is odd behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or odd, the sense of a curious incident.

clue.text: A light basket formed of metal strips

explanation.surface: A lamp consisting of an iron cage.
explanation.definitionFit: An old torch made of an iron cage holding burning fuel, mounted on a pole.

clue.text: What people may do to put a stop to revolutions

definitions.text: What people may do to put a stop to revolutions

parts.words: What people may do to put a stop to revolutions
parts.note: revolutions suggests political uprisings, but here it is turning wheels that are slowed

explanation.definitionFit: Drivers press a pedal to slow the spinning wheels of a vehicle.

clue.text: Turn away from a green

parts.note: taken as written
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Someone told to step back from a village green.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert is the term for green in heraldry, the language of coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert one's eyes is to look aside from something.

clue.text: No practical person wants a fancy table

parts.note: a fancy is a notion or idea
a table of figures or names is a list

explanation.surface: An impractical person desires an elaborate piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy table' looks like ornate furniture, but splits into a notion and a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer devoted to lofty principles is not someone grounded in practicalities.

clue.text: Many a top man with little hesitation gets a stand-in

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
OC is the Officer Commanding, the top man in a unit
um is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Plenty of chief executives who barely pause find a deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary doctor or cleric covering for another is a substitute.

clue.text: The story of a Greek character in the city

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A tale about a Greek figure living in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person but is a letter; EC is the postcode of London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic narrative poem is a kind of tale.

clue.text: Works out manoeuvres

explanation.surface: Trains at the gym, or military drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Works out means does physical training; manoeuvres are military drills or practice operations.

clue.text: Some amerinds quietly and stealthily advance

parts.note: the Cree are a group of Native American peoples
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A band of Native Americans moves forward silently and secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: To move slowly and quietly so as not to be noticed is to sneak forward.

clue.text: Gambling device — a little one requiring a key

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A betting machine needs a small child and a key.
explanation.walkthrough: A tote is the totalisator, the machine that pools bets at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator pools wagers at racecourses and calculates payouts.

clue.text: Regular check into a city's administration

indicators.note: into says the checking word goes inside the other piece
administration suggests the letters are managed into a new order

parts.note: the word city with its s kept as a letter
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: Routine inspection of how a town is run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Administration' signals SYATIC, the letters of 'a city's' rearranged, and 'into' puts the checking word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodical and orderly, following a fixed plan.
